systems.name: ENCHEV AUCTIONS — public-Copart-capability inspired reference architecture
systems.proofPolicy: Blueprint is not implementation, must pass independent CI, legal signoff and sandbox tests
architecturePrinciples: Copart external customer/business capabilities used as reference, no claim that its internal software architecture is public.
PostgreSQL is authoritative for bids, auction ending, winner, ledger and seller debt; Redis and WebSocket are only transport.
All browser/mobile API routes authenticate and authorize on the server; KYC, country and document restrictions apply.
Each auction stores immutable rules/fee snapshots and versions for reproducible final price, taxes and disputes.
Fees in ENCHEV remain unapproved and disabled until signed rate card; Copart prices never become ENCHEV rates.
Documents have traceable version, signer, hash and retention/access policy; PDFs alone are not proof of ownership.
Payment state changes require verified PSP events or dual-controlled bank reconciliation; never mark paid from a browser toggle.
Release gate checks cleared payment, complete originals, country/ELV legality, carrier authority, yard state and one-use PIN.
Production go-live only with signed finance, legal, security and operations approvals. Otherwise sandbox and demo only.
Original 119-day baseline is immutable; this is an additive dependency and implementation checklist.
